argument_summary: The admissible record supports `certify_model` only as a release-readiness decision with an explicit caveat, not as a clean no-material-limitation certification. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports overall launch readiness. The same record also shows an unresolved Spanish-language billing-ticket triage weakness and only a draft mitigation artifact. The packet is therefore supportable if read as preserving certification with required residual-risk documentation, rather than claiming the limitation does not exist.
claims_about_business_cost: No special business-cost claim is needed to justify the narrower reading. The practical point is that a bounded caveat and residual-risk handling are sufficient to avoid unnecessary escalation where the packet already preserves the limitation instead of concealing it.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not support clean certification without material caveats on this record, because there is neither evidence that the weakness is resolved nor an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. But the policy does allow the packet to preserve a narrower position: certification for overall launch readiness while acknowledging that the named-use-case limitation must be disclosed unless covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results support launch readiness; they do not erase the disclosure obligation.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean no-caveat certification.
The Spanish-language billing-support weakness remains unresolved in a named launch use case slice.
The draft runbook is not an approved mitigation under the stated policy because key fields remain TBD.
There is no admissible evidence here of final disclosure text or approved risk acceptance.
